donor_domain: D5_or_economics_renewal_queueing_options (constitutional political economy: Buchanan/Tullock calculus of consent, Brennan-Buchanan reason of rules, Ostrom IAD nested rule levels)
donor_source_ids: Cato Regulation Winter 1987, 'James M. Buchanan: Constitutional Political Economist' (cato.org/regulation/winter-1987/james-m-buchanan-constitutional-political-economist): constitutional choice = choosing rules of the game; post-constitutional = strategy within the game
Buchanan Nobel lecture 1986 (nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/1986/buchanan/lecture/): Wicksellian unanimity shifted to the constitutional stage of choice among rules

Buchanan & Tullock, The Calculus of Consent (oll.libertyfund.org/titles/buchanan-the-calculus-of-consent-logical-foundations-of-constitutional-democracy): external costs + decision-making costs tradeoff determines the optimal majority for collective action
Brennan & Buchanan 1985, The Reason of Rules (OLL Collected Works vol 10)

Voigt 2009, 'Positive Constitutional Economics II' (econstor.eu/bitstream/10419/30109/1/611375176.pdf): section 'Procedural Rules for Changing Rules' — taxonomy of constitutional change via higher-order procedures

Ostrom Workshop IAD guide (ostromworkshop.indiana.edu/pdf/teaching/iad-for-policy-applications.pdf) + McGinnis 2011 'Updated Guide to IAD' (mcginnis.pages.iu.edu/iad_guide.pdf): nested operational / collective-choice / constitutional levels, meta-constitutional level; higher-level rule changes induce lower-level reconfiguration
donor_structure: Three coupled regularities. (1) Level separation (Buchanan/Ostrom): choices form a strict hierarchy — operational moves (strategies within rules) < collective-choice rules (how operational rules are made) < constitutional rules (who may make collective-choice rules); a rule change at level l must be licensed by level l+1. (2) Cost structure (Calculus of Consent): for a collective decision under required consensus q, expected cost = external cost (damage to those bound, DECREASING in q) + decision-making cost (delay/bargaining, INCREASING in q); the sum has an interior optimal q for most decisions — a finite supermajority, not unanimity and not bare majority. (3) Veil rationale (Buchanan/Brennan): constitutional-stage agreement is achievable because choosers are uncertain which position they will occupy; at runtime there is no veil, so interested rule changes need strictly higher bars. The regress 'rules for changing rules for changing rules...' terminates only by an exogenously frozen top level.

mapping: constitutional stage (rules of the game) <-> C_t: the frozen governing layer of the search process
post-constitutional stage (strategy within game) <-> within-run dynamics U, Q_t (G09/G03): moves C_t licenses
collective-choice level (procedural rules for changing rules, Voigt) <-> the amendment process governing C_t -> C_{t+1} at R6
Ostrom nesting (level-l change licensed by level-l+1) <-> amendment licence structure: each C_t change must be licensed by a strictly higher, unchanged layer
external cost (damage from a decision, decreasing in required consensus q) <-> damage from a bad amendment (constitution weakened to admit junk/self-serving changes)
decision-making cost (delay, increasing in q) <-> adaptation lag: stickiness of a constitution that can no longer be corrected within the horizon
veil of uncertainty <-> pre-run freeze conditions (e.g. this D12 protocol itself): rules fixed before the run, where the process has no vested state
infinite regress of rules-for-changing-rules <-> HSG grounding requirement: some level frozen ex ante by construction
preserved_relations: strict level separation: within-run updates (operational) are never self-licensing; every amendment is licensed by a strictly higher, unamended layer — the regress terminates only in a pre-run-frozen level

the Buchanan-Tullock cost tradeoff is a genuine two-sided optimization: an amendment gate has an interior optimal strictness (finite evidence threshold), because both a rubber-stamp gate (external/damage cost) and an absolutist gate (adaptation-lag cost) are dominated

asymmetric legitimacy: pre-run rule choice (veil: process has no vested state) licenses weaker consensus than runtime amendment (interested process) — runtime amendment thresholds must strictly exceed adoption thresholds
known_broken_relations: political economy has human agents with preferences and bargaining; HSG 'consensus' must be reified as verifier/evidence thresholds — without an agent model the supermajority calculus imports costume, not mechanism (costume risk flagged explicitly)

Ostrom levels presuppose an external enforcer/community; HSG has no enforcer outside the run — self-amendment closure is precisely the open problem, consistent with the governance rule that nothing self-promotes/self-signs

the veil argument relies on ex ante uncertainty about one's position; a search process at time t>0 KNOWS its state Sigma_t — design-time legitimacy cannot be recreated at runtime, so runtime amendments can never inherit freeze-strength authority (structural, not operational)
unknown_correspondences: is there a quantitative analogue of the optimal majority q* as a function of amendment damage distribution and horizon (the Calculus-of-Consent minimization carried out on a constitution Markov chain)?

multi-constellation R7: does Ostrom's meta-constitutional level (McGinnis) map to cross-constellation governance, and does any nesting theorem survive when several constellations share modules (G16 R7)?
assumptions_added: amendment damage and adaptation lag are scalar-measurable per amendment event (to make the q-tradeoff well-posed)
the frozen top level is genuinely unreachable by the amendment process within any finite horizon (entrenchment is real, not nominal)
candidate_theorem: A governed time-varying constitution (G08 at R6) is regress-terminating iff some level is frozen pre-run and every amendment licence is strictly level-decreasing; at runtime no amendment can recreate design-time legitimacy (no veil at t>0), so amendment thresholds must strictly exceed adoption thresholds; and under scalar amendment-damage and lag costs there is a finite optimal amendment strictness q* strictly between rubber-stamp and absolute (Buchanan-Tullock form). Corollary matching existing lane-G conditions: ARCHIVE-GOV/EPS-PRECOMMIT pre-commitments in C_t are instances of the frozen top level; removing them dissolves the level separation and makes the amendment process self-licensing.
